Idolize

EYE-duh-lyz · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To idolize to worship greatly or excessively.

Millions of young skaters openly idolize the reigning Olympic gold medalist.

Worked Example

Countless fans idolize the retired quarterback, quoting his interviews from decades ago.

Idolize describes treating a person, often from afar, as a hero worthy of near-worship.

How Idolize Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

worship

worship: regard with adoration

Antonyms

despise

despise: feel contempt for

scorn

How Strong Is It? — admire → lionize → idolize

admire vs. idolize

admire vs. idolize: Admiring someone is respectful and measured; idolizing them crosses into starstruck hero-worship.

lionize vs. idolize

lionize vs. idolize: To lionize someone is to treat them as a celebrity in public, a more social step beyond privately idolizing them.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — idol

root — idol: an image or object of worship (Greek (eidolon))

suffix — -ize

suffix — -ize: to make, to treat as (Greek)

Put it together

Put it together: idol ("an object of worship") + -ize ("to treat as") = to treat someone as an idol.

Use the root in a new word: idolatry

Use the root in a new word: idolatry: The root also survives in "idolatry," the formal word for the worship of images or false gods.
